$comment: The fixed set of views the insight quality pass reviews. Keep the ids stable so a future pass compares against the same views. Chosen to cover the ways generation fails (data shape), not the topic catalogue. See README.md.

views.why: Common topic, state level, race breakdown, full set of groups. The baseline case.
Strong, clear disparity across many counties (matches the card_map_strong_disparity prompt fixture).
Share-vs-population chart; the model must compare shares, not rates (matches the card_pop_vs_distribution fixture).
Multi-year series with every group present; checks trend language without gaps.
Table with rate, share and population columns all present (matches the card_table_full_shares fixture).
Small state, most groups missing across years; the model is most tempted to pad or infer a trend (matches the card_trends_sparse fixture).
Maternal mortality in a small state: one or two groups at most. Checks the model does not invent a comparison.
A single congressional seat: counts of one or zero. A rate of 0 must be cited as a rate, never as nobody.
AHR small-state race groups are largely withheld; few bars, general-population comparison column.
Youth gun deaths in a low-population state: tiny counts, most groups suppressed to a handful of bars.
NCI suppresses small counts; the table shows explicit suppressed rows (matches the card_table_suppressed fixture). The insight must never describe or infer a withheld value.
County map with many grey suppressed counties. Suppressed must not read as zero, low, or missing.
CDC HIV suppresses rural counties. Checks the geographic sentence names only counties with a reported value.
WISQARS suppresses groups under 10 deaths. Bars absent because suppressed, not because the rate is low.
Time series with suppressed years inside a group's line; a gap must not be read as a drop to zero or as a trend.

Single-region county map: only the overall rate is local, so the insight ranks the county against peer counties (matches the card_map_single_region_peers fixture). The sentence must stay ordinal and never quote a peer's rate.
County data from CHR while state data comes from AHR: the population column is all ages here, adults at state level. Checks the comparison base is described correctly.

No pct_share for this topic, so the table compares against the general population (matches the card_table_general_population fixture, at county level). The insight must not present the general population as the rate's own denominator.
Vera county jail data, single-region peer ranking in a large urban county.
Medicare topic with no population column at all (matches the card_table_no_population fixture). Nothing to compare shares against; the model must not manufacture one.
comparegeos with the same group highlighted on both maps: the sentence must center on that group across both places (matches the contrast_compare_geos_active_group fixture).
comparegeos, two states, no highlighted group (matches the contrast_compare_geos fixture).
comparevars across two unrelated measures with a highlighted group: the easiest place to slip in a causal link the data does not support (matches the contrast_compare_vars_active_group fixture).
comparevars, incarceration against poverty nationally; the same view the nightly e2e spec covers, so presence is already asserted and this pass judges only quality.
comparegeos of a state against one of its own counties over time; two sources (AHR vs CHR) with different year coverage.
Full report with every section populated, including age-adjusted ratios (matches the report_full fixture). Four sections, no fallback to partial output.
County report: the geographic section ranks the county against sibling counties rather than child places (matches the report_county_peers fixture).
Report with no age-adjusted section and a general-population comparison (matches the report_no_age_adjusted fixture).
Large unknown-demographic share: the What This Means section must say what share of cases is missing race data and that rates describe only recorded cases.
Suicide by age nationally: the most sensitive topic in the set. Person-first language and no causal claims are the whole test.
